title: Reply to a Guest on Right Mindfulness at the Moment of Death
author: Zhanran
excerpt: The principle of rebirth: right mindfulness at the moment of death, which invites the Buddha's coming to welcome.

inline.s: The principle of rebirth: right mindfulness at the moment of death, which invites the Buddha's coming to welcome.
The Zhongfeng Three Sessions of Contemplation says:

Although it is said that Amitabha gathers sentient beings for rebirth, one must believe that this is only self-manifesting in accordance with the mind, that the sense and the response meet, and that in the end it is not obtained from without.

[Only self-manifesting in accordance with the mind] When Amitabha Buddha comes to welcome (gathers in) sentient beings, this is only self-manifesting in accordance with the mind, not obtained from without. Therefore only the one received can see the Buddha come, while others cannot. [The sense and the response meet] The sense of sentient beings and the response of Amitabha Buddha mutually connect.
Q: As soon as faith is aroused, one attains rebirth. Where then is right mindfulness at death needed?
[Note: As soon as faith is aroused, one attains rebirth is what Master Huijing of the Primal Vow school advocates. He says:
as soon as faith is aroused, one attains rebirth
, and reciting the Buddha's name in daily life is to repay the Buddha's kindness. (from the Essentials of the Pure Land School)]

Answer: As to whether right mindfulness at death is needed, I now quote the instruction of Master Shandao, the second patriarch of the Pure Land school, and Master Yongming, the sixth patriarch; both are manifestations of Amitabha Buddha. Of Master Shandao, Master Yinguang, the manifestation of Mahasthamaprapta, praises him, saying:

The Great Master Shandao is an incarnation of Amitabha; he has great supernatural powers and great wisdom. In his wide exposition of the Pure Land he does not value the mysterious, but only teaches people practice in what is genuine, real, and plain. As for his showing the two practices of the special and the mixed, the benefit is inexhaustible.
(from the Collected Works of Master Yinguang, letter in reply to the householder of Yongjia) Of Master Yongming, Master Yinguang, the manifestation of Mahasthamaprapta, praises him, saying:
Great Master Yongming is an incarnation of Amitabha Buddha; with great compassion he teaches and transforms sentient beings.

(from the Collected Works of Master Yinguang, instruction at the World Buddhist Lay Association) Therefore the birthday of Master Yongming, the seventeenth day of the eleventh lunar month, is taken as the festival of Amitabha's birthday. Since these two great masters are manifestations of Amitabha Buddha, what they say
is the same as what Amitabha Buddha himself proclaimed.
Master Shandao instructs:
At the time when a sickness becomes grave and one is about to die, the relatives must not weep, nor voice sighs of grief and distress, disturbing his mind,
so that he loses his right mindfulness
. They should only all together recite the Buddha's name; only when his breath has ended may they mourn.
If there is even a trace of attachment to this world, it becomes an obstruction and he cannot be liberated
. If one who understands the Pure Land frequently comes to encourage him, this is a supreme good fortune. If one follows this, rebirth is certainly attained, without doubt.
A Text on Right Mindfulness at Death by the Great Master Shandao
) In this Text on Right Mindfulness at Death, Master Shandao continues to instruct:

This method, used by monks, lay people, and those who have not yet recited the Buddha's name, all attain rebirth; there is no doubt. I have often seen worldly people who in ordinary times recite the Buddha's name, praise, and make vows to seek birth in the West with great diligence
(earnest and sincere)
. But when they fall ill they again fear death and say nothing of rebirth and liberation. They wait until the breath fades and life ends,
and the consciousness descends into the dark realm
, and only then begin the ten recitations. This is like locking the door after the thief has gone; what does it avail? The matter of birth and death is great,
one must exert his own strength
. If one thought is mistaken, one suffers for kalpas
; who can take the place of another? Think on it! Think on it! When there is no busyness, one should apply this method
with vigor and uphold it
; this is
the great matter of death
Therefore,
in order to ensure right mindfulness at death,
Master Shandao instructs:
Because the invocation of the name is easy,
if it is sustained, one attains rebirth
. If one can sustain it thought after thought to the end of life, ten in ten are born, a hundred in a hundred are born.

(from the Essentials of the Dharma of Recollection of the Buddha, excerpt of Master Shandao's saying on the special and mixed practice) For the detailed content of the teaching on sustained recitation leading to rebirth, see
Sustained Recitation Leads to Rebirth

[Sustained recitation leads to rebirth] The thought of reciting the Buddha's name is continued thought after thought, and at the end of life one attains rebirth in the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss. Here the sustained means the pure thought continued without interruption spoken of in the Perfect Penetration Chapter of the Recollection of the Buddha by Mahasthamaprapta, that is, the recitation of the Buddha's name continued thought after thought without any stray thought mixing in (if stray thoughts mix in, it is not sustained). This is the state of one mind undisturbed (tied mindfulness without confusion).
Master Yongming instructs:
When practicing the way
(walking meditation)
and in revering and praising, at the time of reciting the Buddha's name and making vows, with utmost sincerity, without any other thought, as if facing execution, as if in prison
(prison: jail)

, pursued by enemies and robbers, pressed by water and fire, single-mindedly seeking deliverance, vowing to escape the wheel of suffering, quickly realizing non-arising, widely saving sentient beings, continuing the Triple Gem, vowing to repay the four kinds of kindness; with such resolve, it will certainly not be in vain. If words and actions do not match
(if words and actions are inconsistent)
, if the power of faith is slight, without a mind of sustained thought after thought, with the intent of frequent interruption
(the recitation interrupted by stray thoughts)

, relying on such negligence, hoping for rebirth at death, one is only obstructed by karmic hindrances, and will hardly meet good friends; pressed by wind and fire, right mindfulness cannot be accomplished. Why?
The present is the cause, death is the fruit
; the cause must be real, then the fruit is not false. If one wishes
the ten recitations at death to be accomplished
, one should prepare in advance the means of passage, accumulate merit, and transfer it to this time; if every thought is not wanting, then there is no worry.
(from the Collected Works of All Good Deeds)
[The ten recitations at death accomplished] Accomplishing the ten recitations sustained at death.
(for details see
The Ten Recitations at Death, Sustained Recitation Leads to Rebirth
[Preparing in advance the means of passage] The means of passage means ferry crossings and bridges; preparing the means of passage means making ready beforehand.

Master Yongming is a manifestation of Amitabha Buddha, and his instruction on the accomplishment of the ten recitations at death also proves that the even up to ten recitations of the Eighteenth Vow of the Sutra on the Buddha of Immeasurable Life refers to the ten recitations at death. And in this instruction Master Yongming spoke of a mind of sustained thought after thought, so the even up to ten recitations in the Eighteenth Vow
is the ten recitations sustained at death
. The Eighteenth Vow says:

If, when I attain Buddhahood, sentient beings of the ten directions, with sincere mind, faith, and joy, desiring to be born in my land, even up to ten recitations; if they are not born there, may I not attain right enlightenment. Except for those who commit the five heinous offenses and slander the right Dharma.
(for the detailed annotation see
The Eighteenth Vow

As for the saying As soon as faith is aroused, one attains rebirth, this is an outright false doctrine. If as soon as faith is aroused one attains rebirth, then why at the end of the Sutra on the Buddha of Immeasurable Life does the Buddha instruct: One should believe and obey,
practice according to the Dharma
? And why in the
Sutra on the Buddha's Reception of the Pure Land
does the Buddha time and again instruct:
practice as said
Why does Master Shandao, the manifestation of Amitabha Buddha, say:
if it is sustained, one attains rebirth
? Why does Master Yongming, the manifestation of Amitabha Buddha, say:
the ten recitations at death accomplished
Q: Is it certain that one attains rebirth by invoking the name?
Answer:
The saying that invoking the name certifies rebirth is very wrong. If invoking the name certifies rebirth, then why in the Sutra on the Buddha's Reception of the Pure Land does the Buddha speak of
tied mindfulness without confusion
, and time and again instruct that one ought to
practice as said
Why does Master Shandao, the manifestation of Amitabha Buddha, say:
if it is sustained, one attains rebirth
? Why does Master Yongming, the manifestation of Amitabha Buddha, say
the ten recitations at death accomplished
? Why does Master Yinguang, the manifestation of Mahasthamaprapta, say:
one who recites with a distracted mind rarely attains rebirth
? (for details see
Does Invoking the Name Certify Rebirth?
The questioner says: The view that with right mindfulness at death the Buddha comes to welcome is wrong; the view that the Buddha comes to welcome and one then dwells in right mindfulness is right.

The Great Master Honen says: Moreover, those who truly have the will to be reborn, who believe in Amitabha's Primal Vow and recite the Buddha's name, have no distress at death. Why? Because the Buddha's coming to welcome is originally for the sake of the practitioner's right mindfulness at death. Those who do not understand this principle all think that they themselves, by their own right mindfulness at death, receive the Buddha's welcome when they recite; this view neither believes in Amitabha's Primal Vow nor understands the scriptures. The Sutra on the Praise of the Pure Land says:
with compassionate protection, causing the mind to be not confused.

Because one recites the Buddha's name constantly in ordinary times, the Buddha certainly comes to welcome; as soon as one sees the Buddha appear, he dwells in right mindfulness. Therefore do not think the recitation is in vain. Those who only pray for right mindfulness at death are greatly mistaken. Thus those who believe in Amitabha's Primal Vow must not have doubt of this kind about the mind at death. For those who recite only at the moment of death, Amitabha has also made the vow of coming to welcome. As for those who attain rebirth by reciting at death, they are evil people who originally had no will for rebirth and had created offenses, but at death met a good advisor and were urged to recite and so were reborn; the Contemplation Sutra also speaks of this. If one is a person who originally recites the Buddha's name, there is no need to insist on the state at death. Because the Buddha's coming to welcome is certain, right mindfulness at death is also certain; this principle should be kept in mind. (from the Collected Works of Master Honen)
Answer:

This passage of the Great Master Honen, by taking excerpts out of context and misconstruing the scriptures, seeks to prove his own view: Because one recites the Buddha's name constantly in ordinary times, the Buddha certainly comes to welcome; as soon as one sees the Buddha appear, he dwells in right mindfulness. And he censures them, saying: Those who do not understand this principle all think that they themselves, by their own right mindfulness at death, receive the Buddha's welcome when they recite; this view neither believes in Amitabha's Primal Vow nor understands the scriptures.
The Great Master Honen's basis is: The Sutra on the Praise of the Pure Land says: with compassionate protection, causing the mind to be not confused.
However, in the Sutra on the Praise of the Pure Land (
the Sutra on the Buddha's Reception of the Pure Land
), the passage with compassionate protection, causing the mind to be not confused reads:

If there are good men or good women of pure faith who, having heard this name of the Buddha of Immeasurable Life with its immeasurable, boundless, inconceivable merits and virtues, and the merits and adornments of the land of Ultimate Bliss, having heard it, reflect upon it, for one day and night, or two or three, or four or five, or six or seven,
in tied mindfulness without confusion
. Then this
(such)
good man or good woman, at the end of life, together with his immeasurable sravaka disciples and the assembly of bodhisattvas, surrounding him front and back,
come and stand before him
, and with compassionate protection,
cause his mind not to be confused
. Having given up his life, he follows the Buddha and the assembly and is born in the pure Buddhafield of the land of Ultimate Bliss of the Buddha of Immeasurable Life.
Here the World-honored One clearly instructs: a good man or woman who recites the Buddha's name in tied mindfulness without confusion (one mind undisturbed),

at the end of life, the Buddha of Immeasurable Life, together with his immeasurable sravaka disciples and the assembly of bodhisattvas, surrounding him front and back, come and stand before him, and with compassionate protection cause his mind not to be confused.
This passage says: Because of
tied mindfulness without confusion
, therefore Amitabha Buddha
comes and stands before him
, and then with compassionate protection,
causes his mind not to be confused
So the World-honored One in this sutra is saying:
in tied mindfulness without confusion
the Buddha
certainly
comes to welcome
. However, the Great Master Honen, taking excerpts out of context and reversing the logic, twists the passage into:
because one constantly recites the Buddha's name, the Buddha
certainly
comes to welcome

. With hidden intent, knowingly and deliberately twisting the scriptures to deceive the faithful — this is the habitual trick of heretical doctrines, and Master Honen and his lineage, down to the present Master Huijing and Master Jingzong of the Primal Vow school, are all the same. For details see Master Jinghui's Essentials of the Pure Land School, Master Jingzong's Master Shandao's Pure Land Thought, Master Jingzong's interview on the Buddhist portal, and other books, videos, and sayings.
What the Great Master Honen says, that
because one constantly recites the Buddha's name
, the Buddha
certainly
comes to welcome, not only does it violate the meaning of the scripture (the Buddha says:
in tied mindfulness without confusion
, the Buddha
certainly
comes to welcome), and is very wrong, but it is also in direct opposition to what Master Shandao instructs:
if it is sustained, one attains rebirth
Master Shandao says:
Just because the invocation of the name is easy,
if it is sustained, one attains rebirth
. If one can
sustain it thought after thought
to the end of life, ten in ten are born, a hundred in a hundred are born.

May all people earnestly reflect: whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying, one must be stern with the mind and restrain oneself, never neglecting by day or night; when the former thought ends in death, the latter thought is born, forever enjoying the unconditioned joy of the Dharma, even up to Buddhahood; is this not a delight!
(from the Essentials of the Dharma of Recollection of the Buddha
excerpt of Master Shandao's saying on the special and mixed practice) For the annotation of this instruction, see
Sustained Recitation Leads to Rebirth

Q: Since this such a good man or good woman has already reached tied mindfulness without confusion, why does it also say that after Amitabha Buddha comes, with compassionate protection he causes the mind not to be confused?

Answer: Tied mindfulness without confusion (one mind undisturbed) is what draws the Buddha to welcome. But this is a shallow level of skill, often not enough to maintain the mind without confusion at the time when the four great elements separate and suffering presses in and demons appear. So Amitabha Buddha, with compassionate protection, causes the mind not to be confused. The Sutra on the Merits of Praising the Buddhas says:
At the time when life is about to end, with single-minded faith and joy, thinking without abandoning or letting go
this is right mindfulness at death
, Amitabha Buddha will
(lead)
the assembly of monks
(the sravaka disciples and assembly of bodhisattvas)
stand before such a person, and the demons at last cannot destroy this
(this good man or good woman)
heart of right enlightenment.
Q: Why do they twist the scriptures to deceive the faithful?

Answer: On the one hand, they use lies to pander to the weaknesses of the faithful, such as the fear of difficulty, the love of easy shortcuts, and the pursuit of worldly pleasures, in order to gain fame and profit. For example, what they advocate: invoking the name certifies rebirth (for details see
Does Invoking the Name Certify Rebirth?
), the gate of the grand vow (for details see
Master Honen Fabricated the Gate of the Grand Vow

), and the evil man as the true object of salvation (maintaining that doing evil and committing crimes does not matter, because the evil man is the true object of Amitabha's salvation; for details see
The Primal Vow School Is a Buddhist-Proclaiming Non-Buddhist Path
), and so on. On the other hand, they often face two great questions from the faithful:
First, how to achieve right mindfulness at death? Second, how to reach one mind undisturbed? (These two questions are the core of Pure Land practice.)

And since they have no real practice themselves, they can only fabricate lies and say: the Buddha will surely come to welcome the one who recites; the Buddha's coming to welcome settles right mindfulness; as soon as faith is aroused, one attains rebirth; invoking the name certifies rebirth;
; and so on. Therefore what need is there for right mindfulness at death? What need for one mind undisturbed?
These people

, in order to win trust, or for fear of being questioned, twist the scriptures and twist the instructions of the patriarchs to conceal their fallacies. Such methods abound in the works, videos, and sayings of the Primal Vow school. And of course there are also those demons of Mara, descendants of the devil, who with hidden intent destroy the Dharma.
Q: In Pure Land practice there is a welter of views, and some even say that the true Pure Land requires no cultivation. Which is right and which is wrong, and how should one judge?
Answer: The view that the Pure Land requires no cultivation is very wrong. At the end of the Sutra on the Buddha of Immeasurable Life the Buddha instructs: One should believe and obey,
practice according to the Dharma
. In the Sutra on the Buddha's Reception of the Pure Land the Buddha time and again instructs:
practice as said

As for how to judge whether the various views on Pure Land practice are right or wrong, one should judge according to the principle of relying on the Dharma and not on a person. What accords with the words and meaning of the scriptures is right; what opposes them is wrong. Empty boasts that cite no scripture are certainly not trustworthy; and even those who cite scripture must be checked to see whether they take excerpts out of context or twist the scriptures (the Master Honen cited above is an example).
In general, heretical doctrines have the following features. First, fabricate out of thin air and make things up. (The gate of the grand vow fabricated by Master Honen is an example; for details see
Master Honen Fabricated the Gate of the Grand Vow
) Second, go round and round, twisting east and west, circling about, so that
people cannot tell which parts are the Buddha's words and which are human words

, and they take fallacy as truth. Third, when citing scripture, twist the passage through taking excerpts out of context and far-fetched interpretation (the Master Honen cited above is an example). Fourth, use the Buddhist scriptures as one's evidence, saying that such and such a sutra says this and that, without appending the original text. If you carefully look up the original, either it is not to be found at all in the sutra they cite, or the original passage has been deliberately altered by them. Observe these features carefully and you will discover them.
The Sutra on the Buddha's Reception of the Pure Land is what the Buddhas of the ten directions praise:
the reception by all Buddhas
Dharma-gate
, which naturally includes Amitabha Buddha of the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss. In it the Buddha says:

Sariputra, in the West there are also present the Tathagata of Immeasurable Life, the Tathagata of Immeasurable Aggregate, the Tathagata of Immeasurable Light, the Tathagata of Immeasurable Banner, the Tathagata of Great Freedom, the Tathagata of Great Light, the Tathagata of Radiance, the Tathagata of the Great Jewel Banner, the Tathagata of Emitting Light, and Buddhas such as these, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, dwelling in their own pure Buddha-lands in the West. Each manifests his broad and long tongue covering the three-thousand great-thousand world, and with it surrounding speaks truthful words: You sentient beings should all believe and receive this praise of the merit and virtue of the inconceivable Buddha-land,
the Dharma-gate of the reception by all Buddhas

Therefore students of the Pure Land should follow the teaching as instructed; what accords with the words and meaning of the Sutra on the Buddha's Reception of the Pure Land is right, and what opposes it is wrong.
Q: What is the core of Pure Land practice?

Answer: The aim of Pure Land practice is to ensure rebirth in the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss at death. Therefore the core of Pure Land practice is to achieve clear right mindfulness at death, without being entangled by mundane conditions or veiled by delusive thoughts. So ordinary practice is to work in the two aspects of longing for that land and wearying of this one, and of one mind undisturbed (tied mindfulness without confusion); at the same time, one must give up evil and do good, so as to prevent karmic hindrances from appearing at death.

There is an old Chinese saying: when the matter arrives, one is no longer in control (if one only starts to make plans when the matter comes, it is too late). If in ordinary times one recites the Buddha's name
without a mind of sustained thought after thought, with the intent of frequent interruption
(the recitation interrupted by stray thoughts)
, how can one at death accomplish the ten recitations sustained?
Therefore the one who recites the Buddha's name must make targeted and adequate preparations in advance
(this is
the core of Pure Land practice
the present is the cause, death the fruit
. Master Yongming, the manifestation of Amitabha Buddha, instructs:
the present is the cause, death is the fruit; the cause must be real, then the fruit is not false
. If one wishes the ten recitations at death to be accomplished
, one should prepare in advance the means of passage, accumulate merit, and transfer it to this time; if every thought is not wanting, then there is no worry.
(from the Collected Works of All Good Deeds)

[The ten recitations at death accomplished] Accomplishing the ten recitations sustained at death. [Preparing in advance the means of passage] The means of passage means ferry crossings and bridges; preparing the means of passage means making ready beforehand.
Q: How does one do the practice of longing for that land and wearying of this one?
Answer: In the
Aware Recitation of the Buddha
, in the chapter on longing and weaning, there is a detailed account of how to cultivate this practice.
Q: How does one reach
one mind undisturbed (tied mindfulness without confusion)?
How can one achieve clear right mindfulness at death?
Answer:
The greatest obstruction to one mind undisturbed (tied mindfulness without confusion) and to
clear right mindfulness at death is stray thoughts. In the
Aware Recitation of the Buddha (abridged)

there is a detailed analysis of the causes of stray thoughts and how to overcome them effectively; it also explains in detail the concrete steps and methods for reaching one mind undisturbed in recitation. As long as one has true faith and a firm vow, works hard and with effort, advances step by step, and persists, one can certainly in ordinary times reach one mind undisturbed in recitation, and at death achieve clear right mindfulness.
Q: If in ordinary times one is fully endowed with faith, vow, and the invocation of the name, is one certain to be reborn at death?
Answer:
Great Master Ouyi, in his Essential Explanation of the Amitabha Sutra, says:
This sutra
(the Buddha Speaks the Amitabha Sutra)
takes faith, vow, and the invocation of the name as the essential of practice. Without faith one cannot arouse the vow; without the vow one cannot guide the practice;
without the excellent practice of the invocation of the name one cannot fulfill the vow and realize what is believed.
As for practice, one holds the name and attains one mind undisturbed.
Therefore, one who truly
is endowed
with faith, vow, and the invocation of the name has certainly reached one mind undisturbed. Otherwise, how could he fulfill the vow and realize what is believed
Since in ordinary times one has reached one mind undisturbed, at death one is certainly able to be reborn.
But it must be noted: if in ordinary times one recites the Buddha's name
without a mind of sustained thought after thought, with the intent of frequent interruption
(the recitation interrupted by stray thoughts)
, that is,
what Master Yongming, the manifestation of Amitabha Buddha,
reproves as
words and actions do not match
(words and actions are inconsistent — one verbally makes vows without the corresponding action to realize them)
, the power of faith is slight
(how can this be called being endowed?)
, relying
on this negligence
(depending on such negligent conduct)
, this is far from being
endowed
with faith, vow, and the invocation of the name, and to hope for rebirth at death is difficult.
Master Yongming instructs:
if words and actions do not match, the power of faith is slight,
without a mind of sustained thought after thought, with the intent of frequent interruption
relying on this negligence
, hoping for rebirth at death, one is only obstructed by karmic hindrances, and will hardly meet good friends; pressed by wind and fire,
right mindfulness cannot be accomplished
. Why?
the present is the cause, death the fruit
, the cause must be real, then the fruit is not false.
If one wishes
the ten recitations at death accomplished
, one should prepare in advance the means of passage, accumulate merit, and transfer it to this time; if every thought is not wanting, there is no worry.
(from the Collected Works of All Good Deeds)
Q: What is the greatest obstruction to Pure Land practice today?

Answer: The greatest obstruction to Pure Land practice today is that the necessity of one mind undisturbed and right mindfulness at death is not yet united in understanding, nor has there been wholehearted effort in expounding, practicing, and exchanging, guiding, and encouraging one another on how to reach one mind undisturbed and how to achieve right mindfulness at death. Hence there is a lack of an excellent practice environment, so that one can only become accomplished through self-study, and the difficulty is far greater.
In fact, as long as one is in an excellent practice environment, reaching one mind undisturbed and achieving right mindfulness at death are not unattainably high,
but are what everyone can accomplish; among ten thousand who practice,
(practicing earnestly)
ten thousand go
. The first patriarch of the Pure Land school, Master Huiyuan, was the first to establish the Lotus Society, setting us a glorious example,
because the theory and method of practice were correct
, the members of the Donglin Lotus Society,
people, each and every one had auspicious signs of rebirth in the Pure Land, and each went most wondrously to be reborn in the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss
[The Donglin Lotus Society]
In the seventh month of the first year of the Yuanxing era of the Eastern Jin (the year
), Master Huiyuan led the two assemblies of monks and lay, in all

people, before the statue of Amitabha Buddha, to hold a fast and make vows together, vowing to be reborn in the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss. Liu Yimin composed the Vow Text. This was the beginning of the Lotus Society, and the Pure Land school is also called the Lotus School. Master Huiyuan led the assembly to form the Lotus Society, practiced recitation with vigor, and dug a pond to plant lotuses; in the water he placed twelve lotuses, which turned with the waves and divided day and night as the measure for the practice of the way, called the lotus clepsydra. Because the theory and method of practice were correct, the

people of the Lotus Society all had auspicious signs of rebirth in the Pure Land. Master Huiyuan, in concentration, several times saw the true body of Amitabha Buddha, and in his later years was told by the Buddha of the time of his passing; when the time came he indeed sat peacefully and passed, going joyfully to the West. [Monks and lay] Black-and-purple is black and plain is white; monks wear black and purple robes, lay people mostly wear white, so monks and lay are called the black-and-white assemblies.
